semanticReview.scope: All 24 baseline and all 24 current displayed name lists were read individually. The review distinguishes a repeated ingredient from a shared broad menu category, related plants with different edible parts, and distinct named bamboo types. A second independent reviewer inspected the current lists.
semanticReview.qualification: Zero confirmed duplicate tasting families is not a claim of completed biological species identification for every historical fishery vernacular name. Unidentified vernacular fish names are not auto-merged without evidence.

catalogChecks.outcome: Both are sourced to Minor Cold, but the ordinary Ganyu strawberry has no usable photo and is absent from both displayed lists. The white strawberry is the displayed representative. Thus this is a duplicate candidate family, not a pre-change displayed duplicate.
No same-term displayed duplicate. Honeyberry / blue honeysuckle is a different fruit and is retained separately.
No same-term displayed duplicate in either 24-term cycle.

intentionalDistinctions.reason: Both are cattail-related vegetables; the catalog documents tender stem core for pucai and new rhizome shoots for caoya. The edible part and form differ, so these are retained as separate tasting choices.
Young lotus rhizome runners and mature enlarged rhizomes are different edible states; the two mature lotus-root entries also occupy different sourced seasons in this cycle.
Male flower stalks and edible kernels are different plant parts. Hickory and walnut are separate foods, not peaches.
The named bamboo types differ and are retained. A location-only spring-shoot name with unresolved bamboo identity is not assumed to duplicate one of the identified types.
The source descriptions distinguish the thin branching white edible underground stems from the segmented spiral tubers; the catalog expressly warns against confusing them.
Flower buds, rose fruit, and ordinary pear fruit are different ingredients; matching the character 梨 alone previously conflated them.

implementationGapsForFutureCatalogGrowth: No shared strawberry, blueberry or grape family rule exists yet. This does not cause a current displayed duplicate, but adding another eligible item in those families would need an explicit review.
